calc-01-c2.text: Gilbert Strang, Edwin Herman et al (2016). Calculus Volume 1, Section 2.2 The Limit of a Function. OpenStax (Rice University).
calc-01-c2.quote: if the limit from the left and the limit from the right take on different values, the limit of the function does not exist.
calc-01-c2.claim: If the two sides don't agree, there's no limit.

calc-01-c3.text: Gilbert Strang, Edwin Herman et al (2016). Calculus Volume 1, Section 2.4 Continuity. OpenStax (Rice University).
calc-01-c3.quote: A function f(x) is continuous at a point a if and only if the following three conditions are satisfied:
calc-01-c3.claim: f(x) is continuous at x = a when three things are true: 1. f(a) exists (the function is defined there) 2. The limit as x approaches a exists

calc-02-c1.text: Matthew Boelkins, David Austin, Steven Schlicker. Section 1.3: The derivative of a function at a point. Active Calculus (Grand Valley State University).
calc-02-c1.quote: A secant line to a curve is simply a line that passes through two points on the curve.
calc-02-c1.claim: We find it by taking two points on the curve, drawing a line between them (a secant line), then sliding the points closer and closer together.

calc-02-c3.text: Matthew Boelkins, David Austin, Steven Schlicker. Section 1.6: The second derivative. Active Calculus (Grand Valley State University).
calc-02-c3.quote: Therefore, on an interval where f'(x) is positive, the function f is increasing (or rising).
calc-02-c3.claim: Where the derivative is positive, the original function is increasing.

calc-03-c1.text: Matthew Boelkins, David Austin, Steven Schlicker. Section 4.2: Riemann sums. Active Calculus (Grand Valley State University).
calc-03-c1.quote: But when the curve bounds a region that is not a familiar geometric shape, we cannot find its area exactly without some key ideas in calculus.
calc-03-c1.claim: A shape with curved edges can't be handled with length × width alone.

calc-03-c3.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Isaac Barrow - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
calc-03-c3.quote: Isaac Barrow was an English mathematician who developed a method of determining tangents that closely approached the methods of calculus, and he was first to recognise that integration and differentiation are inverse operations.
calc-03-c3.claim: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus says: Differentiation and integration are opposites.

calc-04-c1.text: David Guichard. 5.1 Maxima and Minima. Calculus: Early Transcendentals, Whitman College.
calc-04-c1.quote: If (x,f(x)) is a point where f(x) reaches a local maximum or minimum, and if the derivative of f exists at x, then the graph has a tangent line and the tangent line must be horizontal.
calc-04-c1.claim: This works because at a peak or valley, the slope is flat (zero).

calc-04-c2.text: Matthew Boelkins, David Austin, Steven Schlicker. Section 3.1: Related rates. Active Calculus (Grand Valley State University).
calc-04-c2.quote: If two quantities that are related, such as the radius and volume of a spherical balloon, are both changing as implicit functions of time, how are their rates of change related?
calc-04-c2.claim: When two quantities are related and both changing over time, calculus lets us connect their rates of change.

calc-05-c1.text: Matthew Boelkins, David Austin, Steven Schlicker. Section 2.3: The product and quotient rules. Active Calculus (Grand Valley State University).
calc-05-c1.quote: As part (b) of Preview Activity 2.3.1 shows, it is not true in general that the derivative of a product of two functions is the product of the derivatives of those functions.
calc-05-c1.claim: When two functions are multiplied together, the derivative isn't just the product of their derivatives.

calc-05-c2.text: Matthew Boelkins, David Austin, Steven Schlicker. Section 2.5: The chain rule. Active Calculus (Grand Valley State University).
calc-05-c2.quote: is given by the derivative of the outer function evaluated at the inner function, times the derivative of the inner function.
calc-05-c2.claim: Think of it as peeling an onion: differentiate the outer layer, then multiply by the derivative of the inner layer.

calc-06-c1.text: Some Notes on Taylor Polynomials and Taylor Series. University of British Columbia, Department of Mathematics.
calc-06-c1.quote: As well, polynomials are evaluated using the simple operations of multiplication and addition, so it is relatively easy to compute their exact values given x.
calc-06-c1.claim: Polynomials are easy to compute, since they need only addition and multiplication.

calc-06-c3.text: Some Notes on Taylor Polynomials and Taylor Series. University of British Columbia, Department of Mathematics.
calc-06-c3.quote: Here, x is allowed to be any real number since these series converge for all values of x.
calc-06-c3.claim: But eˣ, sin, and cos converge for all x.

calc-07-c1.text: Matthew Boelkins, David Austin, Steven Schlicker. Section 7.1: An introduction to differential equations. Active Calculus (Grand Valley State University).
calc-07-c1.quote: A differential equation is an equation that describes one or more of the derivatives of a function that is unknown to us.
calc-07-c1.claim: A differential equation (DE) is an equation that involves a function and its derivatives.

calc-07-c3.text: David Guichard. 17.5 Second Order Homogeneous Equations. Calculus: Early Transcendentals, Whitman College.
calc-07-c3.quote: A second order differential equation is one containing the second derivative.
calc-07-c3.claim: A second-order DE involves the second derivative.

calc-08-c1.text: David Guichard. 14.3 Partial Differentiation. Calculus: Early Transcendentals, Whitman College.
calc-08-c1.quote: We can save ourselves the effort, small as it is, of substituting k for y: all we are in effect doing is temporarily assuming that y is some constant.
calc-08-c1.claim: When a function has multiple inputs, like f(x, y) = x²y + 3y, we can take a derivative with respect to one variable while holding the others constant.

calc-08-c2.text: David Guichard. 14.5 Directional Derivatives. Calculus: Early Transcendentals, Whitman College.
calc-08-c2.quote: In other words, the gradient ∇ f points in the direction of steepest ascent of the surface, and |∇ f| is the slope in that direction.
calc-08-c2.claim: It points in the direction of steepest ascent.

calc-09-c1.text: Eugene Boman, Robert Rogers (2018). 7.1: Completeness of the Real Number System. Mathematics LibreTexts: Real Analysis (Boman and Rogers).
calc-09-c1.quote: Just like with convergence and continuity, what we need is a rigorous way to convey this idea that the real number system does not have any holes, that it is complete.
calc-09-c1.claim: This is the completeness of the reals: there are no "gaps" for sequences to fall into.

calc-09-c2.text: David Guichard. 11.2 Series. Calculus: Early Transcendentals, Whitman College.
calc-09-c2.quote: A series converges if the sequence of partial sums converges, and otherwise the series diverges.
calc-09-c2.claim: It converges if the partial sums S_N = a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_N approach a finite limit.

calc-09-c3.text: Eugene Boman, Robert Rogers (2018). 8.4: Boundary Issues and Abel’s Theorem. Mathematics LibreTexts: Real Analysis (Boman and Rogers).
calc-09-c3.quote: That is because there is no systematic approach to this boundary problem.
calc-09-c3.claim: On the boundary |x - a| = R, anything can happen.

calc-10-c1.text: David Guichard. 16.5 Divergence and Curl. Calculus: Early Transcendentals, Whitman College.
calc-10-c1.quote: Roughly speaking, divergence measures the tendency of the fluid to collect or disperse at a point, and curl measures the tendency of the fluid to swirl around the point.
calc-10-c1.claim: Measures how much a vector field "spreads out" from a point.

calc-11-c1.text: Jeremy Orloff (2020). 2.6: Cauchy-Riemann Equations. Mathematics LibreTexts: Complex Variables with Applications (Orloff).
calc-11-c1.quote: If u and v satisfy the Cauchy-Riemann equations and have continuous partials then f(z) is differentiable on A.
calc-11-c1.claim: Writing z = x + iy and f(z) = u(x,y) + iv(x,y), a function is holomorphic (complex-differentiable) if it satisfies the Cauchy-Riemann equations.

calc-11-c2.text: Jeremy Orloff (2017). 5.1: Cauchy's Integral for Functions. Mathematics LibreTexts: Complex Variables with Applications (Orloff).
calc-11-c2.quote: This is remarkable: it says that knowing the values of f on the boundary curve C means we know everything about f inside C!! This is probably unlike anything you’ve encountered with functions of real variables.
calc-11-c2.claim: Cauchy's Integral Formula says that a holomorphic function's value at any point inside a contour is completely determined by its values on the contour

calc-12-c1.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Henri Lebesgue - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
calc-12-c1.quote: There is a problem here, namely that a function which is not Riemann integrable may be represented as a uniformly bounded series of Riemann integrable functions.
calc-12-c1.claim: Riemann integration also has problems with limits: the limit of a sequence of Riemann-integrable functions may not be Riemann-integrable, and you can't always interchange limits and integrals.

calc-12-c3.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Henri Lebesgue - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
calc-12-c3.quote: What Lebesgue was able to show was that term by term integration of a uniformly bounded series of Lebesgue integrable functions was always valid.
calc-12-c3.claim: You can freely interchange limits and integrals under a simple boundedness condition.

calc-10-c3.text: Joel Feldman, Andrew Rechnitzer, Elyse Yeager. Section 4.7: A Generalized Stokes' Theorem (optional). CLP-4 Vector Calculus (University of British Columbia), University of Kentucky mirror.
calc-10-c3.quote: As we have seen, the fundamental theorem of calculus, the divergence theorem, Greens’ theorem and Stokes’ theorem share a number of common features. There is in fact a single framework which encompasses and generalizes all of them, and there is a single theorem of which they are all special cases.
calc-10-c3.claim: All three are higher-dimensional versions of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: integral over interior = evaluation on boundary.
